questions.question: A train starting from a railway station and moving with uniform acceleration attains a speed 40 km/h in 10 minutes. Find its acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**185 × 10⁻⁴ m/s².**__

__CONCEPT:__ 

__
 
• The rate of change of displacement of an object is velocity.
 
• The rate of change of velocity of an object is acceleration.
 
• Equations of motion describe the behaviour of a physical system in terms of 'its motion as a function of time'.
 
• If an object is moving with constant acceleration 'a', initial velocity 'u', the first equation of motion gives the final velocity 'v' after a time 't'

v = u + at 

CALCULATION:__

 
• Given, the initial velocity (u) of the train = 0 m/s (at rest)
 
• Terminal velocity (v) of the train = **40km/hour = 11.11 m/s**
 
• Time interval, t = 10 minutes = 600 s.
 
• The First Equations of motion: v = u + at.
 
• The acceleration of the train is given by 

Rightarrow (v - u)/(t) = (11.11 - 0)/(600) = 0.0185

Acceleration** (a) = 185 **×** 10⁻⁴ m/s²**

• **In longitudinal waves, the direction of vibration in the medium of the particle is parallel to the propagation of the wave**.
 
• In **longitudinal waves**, the particles transfer energy from one point to another by vibrating in the line of direction of propagation of the wave.
 
 
• In longitudinal waves, the movement of particles is usually parallel to the movement of energy.
 
 
 
• Here, the particles are also displaced parallel to the direction of the travelling wave.

questions.question: Which defect of vision occurs due to the weakening of ciliary muscles with age?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presbyopia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Presbyopia** is a common age-related vision defect caused by the **weakening of ciliary muscles** and loss of elasticity in the eye's lens.
 
• It typically occurs after the age of **40 years** and progressively worsens with age.
 
• This condition results in difficulty focusing on **nearby objects**, often requiring reading glasses or bifocals for correction.
 
• Presbyopia is a natural part of the aging process and cannot be prevented, but it can be effectively managed with corrective lenses or surgical options.
 
• Unlike other refractive errors, Presbyopia is **not caused by the shape of the cornea or the eyeball**, but by age-induced changes in the eye's focusing ability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness)**

 
 
• It is a refractive error where distant objects appear blurry, caused by the elongation of the eyeball or excessive curvature of the cornea.
 
• It is corrected using **concave lenses** or refractive surgeries like LASIK.
 
 
 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness)**
 
 
• A condition where close objects appear blurry due to the eyeball being too short or the cornea being too flat.
 
• It is corrected using **convex lenses** or surgical options like lens replacement.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• It occurs due to an irregularly shaped cornea or lens, causing blurred or distorted vision.
 
• This condition can affect both near and far vision and is corrected using **cylindrical lenses**.
 
 
 
• **Accommodation of the Eye**
 
 
• The process by which the eye's lens changes shape to focus on objects at varying distances.
 
• Presbyopia occurs when the lens loses this flexibility with age, leading to difficulty in near vision.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the particles of a solid and those of a gas?

options.text: Solid particles move more freely than gas particles.
Solid particles are more closely packed than gas particles
Solid particles have more energy than gas particles.
Solid particles are made of different elements than gas particles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid particles are more closely packed than gas particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Solid particles are more closely packed** than gas particles, leading to a fixed shape and volume for solids.
 
• In solids, the particles are in a fixed, orderly arrangement, **resulting in a rigid structure**.
 
• Gas particles are **spread out and move freely**, leading to no fixed shape or volume for gases.
 
• The close packing of solid particles results in **higher density** compared to gases.
 
• Solids have **lower kinetic energy** in their particles compared to gases, where particles move rapidly and randomly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **States of Matter:**

 
 
• Matter exists primarily in three states: solid, liquid, and gas.
 
• Each state is characterized by different arrangements and movements of its particles.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Gases:**
 
 
• This theory explains the behavior of gas particles, stating that they are in constant, random motion.
 
• The temperature of a gas is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
 
 
• **Density and Volume:**
 
 
• Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
 
• Solids generally have higher density than gases due to closer particle packing.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:**
 
 
• These are forces that hold particles together in a solid or liquid.
 
• In solids, intermolecular forces are strong, giving solids a definite shape and volume.
 
• In gases, these forces are negligible, allowing particles to move independently.

questions.question: Inertia depends on which property of an object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia** is the property of an object that resists changes in its state of motion.
 
• It is directly related to the **mass** of an object; the greater the mass, the greater the inertia.
 
• An object with larger mass requires more force to change its state of motion compared to an object with smaller mass.
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion** states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force, which is a description of inertia.
 
• For example, a heavy truck has more inertia than a small car, making it harder to start moving or stop once in motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shape**__

 __
 
• The **shape** of an object does not affect its inertia. Inertia is solely dependent on mass.
 
• For example, a cube and a sphere of the same mass will have the same inertia regardless of their different shapes.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration**__
 __
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity of an object, not a property that affects inertia.
 
• While acceleration can change the motion of an object, it doesn't determine the object's inertia.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**__
 
 
• **Velocity** is the speed of an object in a particular direction, and it does not influence the inertia of the object.
 
• An object's inertia remains the same irrespective of its velocity.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 3/4 : 5/8 : 7/12. If the difference between the greatest and the smallest number is 48, then the value of the greatest number will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert the fractional **ratio** to a simple integer ratio by multiplying with the **LCM** of denominators (4, 8, 12) = 24.

The simplified ratio becomes 18 : 15 : 14.

**Difference** between the **greatest** (18 units) and **smallest** (14 units) = 4 units.

Given 4 units = 48 ⇒ 1 unit = 12.

**Greatest number** = 18 units = 18 × 12 = 216.

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of three numbers = 3/4 : 5/8 : 7/12

Difference between **greatest** and **smallest** = 48

**Formula Used:**

To simplify a fractional ratio, multiply each term by the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the denominators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb1ebb7ca76bb1d50117e006fedab6764b7a43f23c7848c4cf4522b9924081ce.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **LCM** of denominators (4, 8, 12) = 24

⇒ First number = 3/4 × 24 = 18x

⇒ Second number = 5/8 × 24 = 15x

⇒ Third number = 7/12 × 24 = 14x

⇒ **Simplified Ratio** = 18 : 15 : 14

⇒ **Greatest** = 18x, **Smallest** = 14x

⇒ 18x − 14x = 48

⇒ 4x = 48

⇒ x = 48 ÷ 4 = 12

⇒ Value of the **greatest number** = 18x = 18 × 12 = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simplification of Fractional Ratios

To convert fractions a/b : c/d to integers, multiply each by the LCM of b and d. This maintains the **proportional relationship** while easing calculations.

If the difference between two ratio parts is known, the value of one part is calculated as (Actual Difference) ÷ (Difference in Ratio Units).

questions.question: The three medians RQ, SP, and TN of ΔRST intersect at point O. If the area of triangleRST is 48 cm², then the area of the quadrilateral SQON is:

The **three medians** of a triangle divide it into **6 smaller triangles of equal area**.

The **quadrilateral SQON** is composed of exactly 2 of these small triangles (ΔSOQ and ΔSON).

Area of ΔRST = 48 cm²

RQ, SP, and TN are the medians intersecting at the **centroid O**.

The **centroid** of a triangle divides it into three triangles of equal area, and each median divides the triangle into two equal areas. Consequently, the three medians divide the triangle into **six triangles of equal area**.

questions.question: If x - (1)/(2x) = 4, the the value of rm8x³ - (1)/(x³) will be :

questions.question: What does privatisation mean in the Indian economic context?

options.text: Selling government companies to private companies

__
 
• **Privatisation** refers to the process of transferring ownership and control of public sector enterprises or government-owned assets to private entities.
 
• It aims to improve efficiency, profitability, and competitiveness by reducing government interference and encouraging private sector management.
 
• In India, privatisation started gaining momentum during the **1991 economic reforms**, following the liberalisation policy to boost economic growth.
 
• Examples of privatisation in India include the sale of government stakes in entities such as **Air India, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), and VSNL**.

• **Disinvestment**: This involves selling a portion of government equity in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to private investors, often retaining majority ownership.
 
• **Strategic Sale**: A form of privatisation where the government sells a significant portion or full ownership of a PSU to a private entity, transferring management control.
 
• **Liberalisation**: Refers to the relaxation of government restrictions in areas such as trade, investment, and industrial policies to promote private sector activity.
 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**: These are companies owned by the government, which may be fully or partially privatised to improve efficiency and profitability.
 
• Privatisation can lead to increased competition, better services, and more job opportunities, but critics argue it may also result in reduced focus on social welfare and higher costs for essential services.

questions.question: Technological innovation was key to the success of the Green Revolution. The success of HYV seeds in India was contingent on which critical input?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical fertilisers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Technological innovation** played a pivotal role in the success of the **Green Revolution**, particularly in countries like India. The introduction of **High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds** significantly boosted agricultural productivity.
 
• The success of HYV seeds was contingent upon the availability of **chemical fertilisers**, as these seeds required higher inputs of nutrients to achieve their full yield potential.
 
• **Chemical fertilisers** provided essential nutrients such as **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K)** to crops, which are critical for growth and high yields.
 
• India saw a dramatic increase in food grain production during the Green Revolution period (1960s-70s) due to the combined use of **HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, and advanced irrigation techniques**.
 
• Other inputs like **forest cover, hand tools, and organic compost** were not sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of HYV seeds, making **chemical fertilisers** indispensable for their success.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Chemical fertilisers**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **High Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**

 
 
• HYV seeds were first introduced in India during the **1960s** as part of the Green Revolution.
 
• These seeds were developed to produce more grains per hectare compared to traditional seeds.
 
• They required intensive agricultural inputs such as **chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and regular irrigation** for maximum productivity.
 
• Examples include wheat varieties like **Kalyan Sona** and **Sonora 64**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chemical Fertilisers:**
 
 
• Fertilisers supply essential nutrients like **nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium**, which are vital for plant growth and development.
 
• The use of chemical fertilisers in India saw a significant increase during the Green Revolution, contributing to the country’s ability to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.
 
• India became one of the largest producers of food grains globally due to the use of fertilisers.
 
• Popular fertilisers include **urea (nitrogen), DAP (diammonium phosphate), and potash**.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution in India:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the **1960s and 1970s** when India achieved rapid agricultural growth by adopting modern farming techniques.
 
• Key aspects included the introduction of HYV seeds, expansion of irrigation facilities, and use of fertilisers and pesticides.
 
• It was spearheaded by **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan**, often referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India."
 
• States like **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh** were the major beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Organic Compost:**
 
 
• While organic compost is beneficial for soil health, it lacks the high nutrient concentration required for HYV seeds to achieve their potential yields.
 
• Organic compost provides nutrients slowly over time, which is insufficient for the intensive needs of high-yield crops.
 
• It is not a substitute for chemical fertilisers in large-scale agriculture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Forest Cover:**

 
 
• Forest cover helps in maintaining ecological balance, but it does not provide the nutrients required for HYV seeds.
 
• It plays a role in water conservation and climate regulation but is unrelated to the Green Revolution’s technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Hand Tools:**
 
 
• Traditional hand tools were inadequate for large-scale farming during the Green Revolution.
 
• Modern machinery like tractors and harvesters replaced hand tools for efficient farm management.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• India achieved self-sufficiency in food grains, reducing dependence on imports.
 
• It led to socio-economic changes, including improved incomes for farmers and reduced poverty in rural areas.
 
• However, it also caused environmental concerns such as soil degradation, water pollution, and overuse of chemical fertilisers.

The expenses of the Union Public Service commission including any salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the members or employees of the Commission shall be charged on which of the following?

I Consolidated Fund of India

II. Contingency Funds of India

__
 
• The **Consolidated Fund of India** is one of the most significant accounts of the Government of India.
 
• It comprises all **revenues (tax and non-tax)** received by the Government of India, all loans raised, and all money received by repayment of loans.
 
• Expenses related to the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**, including salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to members and employees, are charged on this fund.
 
• Being a charged expenditure, these expenses are not subject to the **vote of Parliament**. This ensures the **independence and autonomy** of UPSC.
 
• The provision for charging these expenses is made under **Article 322** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This constitutional safeguard reinforces the importance of UPSC in maintaining a fair and transparent recruitment process for civil services.

• The amount spent from this fund must later be authorized by Parliament and replenished.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. A solar eclipse- The Moon caste a shadow on Earth when it comes between the Sun and Earth.

2. A lunar eclipse- During the new moon phase, the Moon passes through the Earth's shadow.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) 1 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1** is correct: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting its shadow on Earth.
 
• **Statement 2** is incorrect: A lunar eclipse occurs during the full moon phase, not the new moon phase, when the Moon passes through Earth's shadow.
 
• During a solar eclipse, the Sun appears partially or completely obscured as seen from Earth due to the Moon's shadow.
 
• Lunar eclipses happen only when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align perfectly in a straight line, with Earth in the middle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar Eclipse:**

 
 
• Occurs during the new moon phase when the Moon blocks sunlight from reaching Earth.
 
• The three types of solar eclipses are total, partial, and annular.
 
• A total solar eclipse occurs when the Moon completely covers the Sun, casting a shadow on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Lunar Eclipse:**
 
 
• Occurs during the full moon phase when Earth casts its shadow on the Moon.
 
• The two types of lunar eclipses are total and partial, depending on the extent of the Earth's shadow covering the Moon.
 
• The reddish appearance of the Moon during a total lunar eclipse is due to Earth's atmosphere scattering sunlight, known as the "blood moon" effect.
 
 
 
• **Phases of the Moon:** The Moon goes through eight phases (new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent) in its monthly cycle.
 
• **Alignment (Syzygy):** A solar or lunar eclipse can only occur during syzygy, when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align in a straight line.
 
• **Umbra and Penumbra:**
 
 
• The umbra is the darkest part of the shadow where the Sun is completely blocked.
 
• The penumbra is the lighter shadow where the Sun is only partially obscured.

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most prominent cultural festival of Assam, celebrated with enthusiasm by all communities.
 
• The festival marks the **harvest season** and is celebrated to express gratitude to nature and honor the hard work of farmers.
 
• There are three main types of Bihu – **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Magh Bihu** (Bhogali Bihu), and **Kati Bihu** (Kongali Bihu).
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, celebrated in April, marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the sowing season.
 
• **Magh Bihu**, celebrated in January, marks the end of the harvesting season and is accompanied by feasting and bonfires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rongali Bihu:** Celebrated in April, this is the most vibrant and widely celebrated Bihu. It marks the Assamese New Year and the start of the agricultural cycle.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:** Also known as Magh Bihu, it is celebrated in January after the harvest, signifying a time of abundance and community feasting.
 
• **Kongali Bihu:** Celebrated in October, this marks the end of the sowing season and is a quieter festival with prayers for a good harvest.
 
• The word "Bihu" originates from the Sanskrit word "**Vishuv**", signifying the solar equinox. It is closely tied to the agrarian lifestyle of Assam.
 
• During Bihu, traditional folk dances and songs like the **Bihu dance** and **Bihu geet** are performed to celebrate joy and prosperity.
